blocks.body: # PN2D general-Tri3 avalanche Tasks 1-10 completion and physics summary

## Technical summary
Tasks 1-7 and Task 10 completed their planned evidence, implementation, or decision work. That does not mean all gates passed: Task 6 failed the true-relative source-Jacobian gate and Task 7 failed the cross-topology QFP-causality gate. Therefore Tasks 8-9 were correctly not entered. The approved production decision is to keep `element_edge_sg_gss_laux` opt-in and diagnostic-only, with no change to Van Overstraeten, the global QFP-gradient driver, or any production default.
## The execution stopped at two independent authorization gates

## Scope and metric definitions
The fixed-state lattice covers exact imported states at -1, -10, and -20 V. Density and source errors are reported in dex; vector, closure, and Jacobian errors are dimensionless relative errors. `Sent box` means a documented box-operator reconstruction and is never labeled native directed-edge current. Candidate/production QFP ratios below one mean improvement. The constrained-obtuse mesh is diagnostic-only.

## Imported density and P1 vectors pass before current support is evaluated
The upstream transformation is not the limiting physics: carrier density, electric field, and electron/hole QFP gradients all satisfy their frozen gates on coarse, acute-skewed, and constrained-obtuse states.

## Current medians pass on scientific meshes, but tails and global closure fail
The GSS/Laux matching-support median current errors pass on coarse and acute-skewed meshes, while P95, sign, terminal-current, and KCL gates do not. The constrained-obtuse case additionally exposes the pre-fix Vela area defect.

## Coarse source support closes, while the acute-skewed source remains outside the general gate
ReadMeasure versus CurrentPlot closes at machine precision on both scientific meshes. Reconstructed box current closes the coarse source but not the skewed source, so changing alpha or fitting a scale is not authorized.

## The opt-in operator improves coarse QFP updates but worsens Minimal6 at the first material bias
At -10 V, every coarse residual/update group improves, while every Minimal6 group worsens. This cross-topology contradiction prevents a causal claim that source support generally fixes QFP evolution.
## Task 8 authorization fails independently on Jacobian parity and QFP causality

## Methodology and robustness
Evidence used two independently generated roots with matching hashes. The final verifier does not import analyzer calculations; it validates both 117-configuration roots, exact coarse fields, topology, path bindings, complete input hashes, paired avalanche-off/SRH-off controls, residual closure, Jacobian gates, authorization, and typed outcome. Independent scientific and code reviews found no remaining blocking inconsistency after the true-relative Jacobian correction.

## Limitations and uncertainty
There is no documented native general-Tri3 directed-edge current or native element-alpha observation, so those comparisons remain `insufficient_native_observation`. Element-local reconstructed flux is not the native global Sentaurus continuity operator. The obtuse normalization proves nonnegative exact-area closure, not native local-support parity. No Task 8 self-consistent curve or Task 9 physical BV curve exists because entry was not authorized.

## Recommended next step
Keep the candidate opt-in and diagnostic-only. The next scientific work should explain the isolated source-Jacobian mismatch and the topology-dependent -10 V QFP response using a new independent observation or operator derivation. Do not tune field, mobility, alpha, geometry scale, or the production default to force agreement.

## Further questions
Can a documented native Sentaurus observation disambiguate element alpha or directed current support? Which local derivative term produces the 0.964 source-Jacobian discrepancy? Why does the same support change improve coarse7x3 but worsen Minimal6 at -10 V? Until those questions are resolved, self-consistent and BV execution remains out of scope.
